title: Haman
lead: Haman son of Hammedatha, called "the Agagite" and "the enemy of the Jews," was King Ahasuerus's chief official. Angered when Mordecai would not bow, he cast lots and won a decree to destroy every Jew in the empire, and was hanged on the pole he had set up for Mordecai.

sections.h: Haman in the Bible and after
sections.b: Haman appears only in Esther. The king raises him above all his officials (Esther 3:1); Mordecai's refusal to bow fills him with rage, and he plans to destroy all of Mordecai's people (Esther 3:5–6). He casts Pur, the lot (Esther 3:7), offers 10,000 talents of silver for the decree (Esther 3:9), and later builds a pole to hang Mordecai (Esther 5:14). His fall comes at Esther's second feast (Esther 7), and his ten sons die in Adar (Esther 9:7–10). His title "the Agagite" links him to Agag, the Amalekite king Saul spared (1 Samuel 15:8–9), and Jewish tradition reads the conflict as the last round of Israel's war with Amalek (Exodus 17:16; Deuteronomy 25:17–19); see Amalek. The Greek Esther calls him a "Bougaean" and, in the king's second letter, a Macedonian. At the Purim reading, listeners drown out his name with noise.
